Messages.Author: Thrall of Arika
Messages.Body:
On Nov 4, 4:05 am, "Orpheus" <orpheus...@NOSPAMfree.fr> wrote:
> Thrall of Arika wrote:
> > Because Protean combat ends is much more effective than this Obfuscate
> > one, perhaps?
>
> Not compared to the changes in crypt necessary. If I can play 7-8-Caps
> rather than 10-Caps I'm more than ready to pay 1 blood each S:CE, and choose
> guys with sup Obf (they'll probably have it anyway, while when you must add
> Pre or Pro they don't always).

That's certainly a fair point. If you're just grafting on Protean/
Presence strictly for combat ends, then yes, that's a concept that is
likely not to be as effective now. But you weren't making a deck to
use Protean, you were making a malkavian deck that could S:CE. How you
got it didn't matter (considering you have been trying both). Now you
can instead focus on using Malkavians you want, rather than being
forced to use the ones who happen to have Protean/Presence out-of-
clan. I still fail so see how this is bad. Now, the combination of
everything for one clan, as you discuss below, I can see as more of a
concern.

> > Protean offers more varied stealth to add to your
> > stealth pool.
> > If you have sufficient blood gain, you can go ahead and
> > make your bleeds unblockable ... add in surprise aggravated damage ...
>
> Annecdotical compared to what Obf can do by itself. Not to mention that most
> Malks (for instance) will have inferior Pro, which isn't that good for
> stealth.

I'm not saying that people graft on Protean to do all these things,
just that the options are there. If you are using Protean, you can
make use of the entire discipline, not just use it for Earth Meld.
Heck, you can add in Homunculi so that your bleeders can untap to
Misdirect .. that would certainly be a strong effect for the deck.

> > The addition of No Trace has no real effect on making your Malkavian
> > Protean deck. People design such decks for the challenge of it, not
> > that Malkavians desperately need to have combat ends to survive.
>
> Sorry to say that this statement is wrong. "People" make decks to win, at
> least good players do and even more so in tournament. Of course some of us
> want to have fun too, but if the "challenge" just consists in making a deck
> the hard way when it can work much better without complicating things, very
> few players will choose to go that way, for understandable reasons.
>
> And I've seen titled Malks decks where Pro was added solely "to survive"
> rush decks (those without IG obviously, but it's quite efficient against
> rushing allies).

Well, we just have different views. If you are just concerned with
winning, and S:CE was viewed as your best defense, then you should be
making a Setite deck, not a Malkavian one. Your choice, however, was
to go a more difficult, challenging route by using a rare out-of-clan
discipline to augment your deck with S:CE.

> > Why? Fortitude offers you all you want and more. Much better and
> > varied damage prevention,
>
> You don't need it, you steal blood. One prevent card (two with Glancing
> Blow) is enough to make the difference.
>
> > Freak Drives,
>
> You don't need it, you have Rutor's Hand.

If you can get the action off ... and can afford the 4 blood/going to
torpor. It's just that in my mind if you're going to go through the
trouble of grafting on a discipline, you should be making use of that
discipline. Heck, Theft is near good enough as a prevent until you hit
someone with some combat. Glancing Blow is only good for defense
against Aggro Poke, with a high cost (not replacing until your untap).

> Anyway, my point exactly : those options are now not interesting enough
> anymore to go into the trouble of an alternative crypt. All because of one
> small card. And there are several like that in the set.

How is it interesting that if I want to have a Thaumaturgy deck that
can prevent, I basically have 8 Tremere/!Tremere to choose from before
using discipline skills (skipping Kyoko since she has no Thaum to
speak of)? Of which I can't even use all of them due to grouping. I
could go out of clan, certainly, and stock up on 9+ caps, but even
then it leaves me with a very small selection.

It just seems we have different views on what is 'interesting'. I can
certainly see the appeal of a deck-building challenge, I do it far too
often myself. But I find it just as interesting to have an option to
use vampires I wouldn't have considered before because I now don't
have to look for obscure out-of-clan disciplines, and then build decks
around those particular vampires because of the need of the grafted on
discipline.

> > etc. Just because there is a prevent now for Thaumaturgy doesn't mean
> > you have to rush out and only use it. Again, it's the challenge of
> > making the deck work in the first place, which this card has no
> > bearing on.
>
> No. The challenge is making the best possible deck in a given concept. If
> your concept is Dawn Op / Weather Control, you need For. If it is anything
> else, you just don't need For anymore and it would be silly to go for a
> considerably bigger crypt just to add difficulty (or maybe you're so much
> better than the rest of your playgroup and you want added handicap ? Maybe
> you can play Laibon with a hand tied behind your back ?).

Well, the specific combo mentioned here requires Fortitude for the
actual combo, not to prevent. And Rego Motus won't help this deck
concept at all, at least in regards to preventing the aggravated
damage from Weather Control. And since you're using Fortitude as a
main concept for the deck, the Fortitude prevents will serve you much
better for any potential hit back than Rego Motus will.

But I can see what you're saying. As with most any expansion, decks
ideas and concepts will change. Some become more effective, others
less so. It's inevitable. Lazvernius used to be a popular rusher
around here way back when, but fell to the wayside, especially with
Enkidu's arrival. Still, it doesn't mean you can't make an effective
Laz rush deck, just that there are other, potentially more potent (pun
intended) versions out there.

> > In the end,
> > what other decks can do isn't at all a concern. Unless you're holding
> > some theme night where you know what kind of deck you're facing, what
> > does it matter if someone brings their Setite stealth/bleed with
> > Presence combat ends, or their new Nosferatu stealth/bleed with
> > Obfuscate combat ends?
>
> Nosferatu stealth / bleed ? That must be good ! Let me pick Setites
> please... ;)

That's my point. People laugh at the concept of Nosferatu stealth
bleed, because currently, though they certainly have the stealth, they
have little bleed punch, unlike other Obfuscate clans. Yes, they can
tool up with equipment/retainers, but then so can the other clans, who
still have their discipline punch cards. Sure, +1 bleed is pretty much
a dime a dozen nowadays, but it at least provides some bleed potential
for a few clans that are noticeably lacking in it.

> As for S:CE for Nosferatu, it's more of a problem with the current Tier1
> deck in that clan : Nosfe Princes. But they already have a S:CE now, so...
> Sure, in the swiss version of the deck the goal was to go fast, so there is
> no combat at all in it, but in an environment with, say, lots of Shamblings
> (happens a lot here) a few S:CEs might just save the day. Too late to beat
> that particular horse now anyway, but the example is still valid.

Yes, so if the 'fast' Nos Princes deck starts packing No Trace to
defend itself, it starts losing speed as card slots are taken up with
defense, rather than offense. And now Nos Princes have an option to
play defensively in combat, rather than hoping their offensive combat
scares people off.

> >> Less skill, more randomness.
>
> > Don't agree with this logic. Going into a tournament, you have no idea
> > what you're going to face in your opponents. More varied available
> > deck types doesn't make it any more random in what you'll face as it
> > did before.
>
> That is where you don't understand my point. I'm not talking more varied
> archetypes, which is good !!! I'm talking inpredictability of disciplines
> because of their flattening, which in my opinion is bad. Very different
> things. Do you see the difference ?

I can see the difference, I just don't agree that it's bad. To me,
predictability is bad. I shouldn't be able to guess what your deck can
do upon seeing one vampire, or one discard. I should be forced to be
on my toes. If I see Nossies, I shouldn't be thinking "great, don't
have to worry about dealing with bleeds".

But my statement wasn't to do with the predictability of disciplines,
it was in regards to making a deck. What other decks can and can't do
doesn't matter when you're building your deck. The fact that Obfuscate
has a Combat Ends doesn't matter, since you could just as easily have
faced a Presence deck with Combat Ends, or a Protean one. If your deck
isn't designed to handle combat ends, then what does it matter how
that combat ends comes about?

Now I do agree that it affects your own deck design options. Most any
new card will do that, so moreso than others (i.e. Vessel).

> > Sure, and as I said, 3/4 of the vampires go unused (An exaggeration,
> > of course, but not too far off the mark. I've not used about 11 out of
> > 48 Tremere, and that's because I play Tremere a lot. I've used 23 of
> > 48 Nosferatu, most of which haven't been used since Jyhad), because
> > they're not worth the effort to graft on the desired discipline to
> > survive combat, say, or to get S:CE. The game currently is based
> > around a pool of a select few number of vampires, with random weenies
> > thrown in for support, and a large chunk of vampires we could get more
> > use out of decorating things with than playing.
>
> Agreed, although some crypts are much better than others (the !Malks or
> Trems/!Trems have pretty good overall crypts !!).

Yes, there are a lot of good choices. And I do agree with you that
people will still use these good vampires with the new cards. I do
think though, that we'll be using more of our vampires overall,
though, since they can now more easily fit in with some deck ideas.

> DI is and has always been a no-brainer, it _abstains_ people from adapting,
> because it does everything by itself. But it can thwart a good plan, still
> all by itself, and now it isn't even possible to plan it better by keeping
> another copy of the card in hand. It is a silver bullet. That cannot be
> good.

I can see what you're saying, but I can't really feel sorry for
Malkavian bleed decks that are forced to maybe wait an extra turn to
oust. I really can't. If your deck is a one-trick pony, that's the
price you pay if something gums up the works.

> > Certainly there are some good cards,
> > that will likely become staples in a number of decks. But I haven't
> > really seen anything that is going to overshadow any of the tried and
> > true decks out there. I think it's more the case where there will be
> > _more_ tried and true concepts added to the mix, which to me is a good
> > thing.
>
> Then you didn't read any of what I said, because I listed a few concepts
> which are dead now.

The concept isn't dead, just the particular method. You still have
your Malkavian stealth/bleed with combat ends deck. It's just using
Obfuscate now, instead of Protean/Presence. Now, if your goal was to
make a Protean Malkavian deck, that's something different.

> > As for the Carna scenario, the new Auspex card doesn't give anything
> > to Carna she didn't already have access to, and better (Enhanced
> > Senses already gave her +2 intercept, without any limitation).
>
> It's cumulative. It gives +2 int to weenie Aus with inferior discipline. It
> does change things.
>
> > Yes,
> > the superior gives a wake, but then she can't use another for the +2
> > intercept.
>
> Poor girl !! Where will she find that cept now ?! Oh, but wait...
>
> > And the Tremere ally, while a neat concept, doesn't truly
> > add much more to the mix. It's just another way to get intercept that
> > could have come from intercept locations, Bowl and retainers, or
> > transient Auspex cards.
>
> Waht you're saying is : Bowl doesn't make a big enough diffence ; the Aus
> card neither ; and the ally neither. Let's admit you're right. Now let's put
> all of those together, plus Carna and co, and we have ? A stealther's worst
> nightmare !!

Certainly, Carna was already a stealther's worst nightmare. The
addition of another +2 intercept (conditional on it being directed) I
don't think changes things. She could already pack on Mr. Wintrop,
Sports Bike, Bowl, Corpse Minion, Enhanced Senses, Spirits Touch,
Precognition, Burnt Offerings, Eagle's Sight, Melange, My Enemy's
Enemy, Telepathic Misdirection, Sins of the Cauchemar, plus a slew of
intercept locations, Biothaum Experimenting and gaining Raptors or
Raven Spies. All of which help against Vote decks, blocking equips/
recruits, etc. Sure, Eye of Argus could be thrown in to the mix, but
do you really think it's changing the fact that Carna can be an
impassable intercept wall?

The most likely use of the card is the superior, which gives you a
Wake without the drawback. But then, it should be more potent, as it
requires AUS, rather than being disciplineless. It'll also help out
clans who have aus out-of-clan, in better defending themselves.

> I agree that BDs aren't wallpaper yet, but they certainly have become much
> scarcer in play.

I guess it's just because it hasn't happened here. I mean certainly,
people play Vessels, but I know for myself that more than once I'd
have preferred a Blood Doll over Vessel in my hand. That fact alone
will keep me playing Blood Dolls, even at the risk of getting removed
later on.

> > No
> > Trace will help Obfuscate decks be more defensive, but it's not going
> > to do anything that's not already available, just open up the options
> > for it.
>
> Ease them up a lot ! Believe me, I've juggled with Pre in a Dem deck, it's
> easier said than done !!

To play Devil's Advocate here .. why bother? You have perfectly good
stealth/bleed with S:CE with Setites.

> > Now if I want to play stealth/bleed with a S:CE angle, I don't
> > have to turn to the Setites, or graft on Presence or Protean.
>
> You can just play the more versatile bleed discipline, the one that can let
> you threaten who you want on the table, and all that in a deflecting clan.
> How is that good ? Do you imply that this just killed Setite S'n'B too ? ;)

No, by the simple fact that No Trace isn't as good as Presence or
Protean combat ends. Sure, your Malkavian gets out of combat, and
that's about it. Setites and bleeding Gangrel have the option to go do
something else, or defend the homefront more easily by virtue of being
untapped (or for Setites, to gain more bleed, or do damage to the
opposing minion).

> > With the
> > animalism bleed card, Nossies can now actually compete a bit more on
> > the bleed part as with Setites,
>
> Far from it

I did said "a bit", not that they would be on the same level.

> > Assamites and Gangrel.
>
> I don't see the link with those 2 ??

Assamites now make strong stealth/bleeders ... gangrel have strong
stealth/combat ends. Nossies have ... well, stealth out the wazoo, and
not much else (in regards to bleeding and combat defense). They have
great offense combat-wise, but if the deck isn't fighty, their only
option was to hope they could out-maneuver their opponent, and that
they didn't then have ranged combat.

> > I think it's
> > great that now if you see a Nossie, it's not automatically going to be
> > either a weenie animalism deck or a Princes deck.
>
> I don't think that a +1 bleed will open a new concept, you could already do
> that disciplineless. The rush / bleed option is certainly a good option, it
> is just thematically wrong in my book. But it is now the worst of the cited
> cards in the lot for me ! As a matter of facts, if there had just been one
> or two such cards in the set it would have been unconspicuous, as were sonar
> and co. But there are a lot of them, and the message seems to be : "we don't
> care about the meaning of the disciplines anymore". And that is what I
> disclike.
>
> Wow, that was long (as was your previous answer). Hope it helps you
> understand My PoV at least.
>
> Cheers,
>
> Orpheus

I do, I do agree that you make some valid points, and have some valid
concerns. Without seeing the whole set of cards, it's hard to say.
While some cards do add new abilities to disciplines, it's hard to
tell if such cards will really have that huge an impact. While I can
certainly see No Trace adding to Malkavian decks, evidence has shown
that Malkavian decks have done just fine without such combat defense.
The same for Rego Motus for Tremere, though again (despite personal
experience), they have stood up relatively well without prevent. Will
these cards make these decks stronger? More than likely. But it's not
as if these are totally foreign concepts, it'll just now be easier to
build such deck concepts, especially for those with smaller card
pools.

Will it be game breaking? I highly doubt it. Even the cards I thought
were "holy cow, what were they thinking", on reflection, simply strong
cards, and not the end of the game a we know it.

Chris, Thrall of Arika

>
> The game theory is this:
>
> 1) If enough people are playing Vessel to counter Blood Dolls (which
> is what you're saying), eventually people will give up on Blood Dolls
> entirely.
> 2) Vessel isn't generally a very good card if no one is playing Blood
> Dolls.
> 3) Because of #2 above, people will begin looking to non-Blood Doll,
> non-Vessel sources of poolgain.
> 4) If enough people use NBDNV sources of poolgain, people will stop
> playing Vessel (again, because of #2 above).
> 5) At this point, Blood Doll can come back into usage, and the cycle

I understand this reasoning but I disagree with it (actually, I was
more or less addressing this in the quoted paragraph... ;) ).

First I beleive Vessel isn't such a terrible card. So even if the game
had no Blood Doll at all, people would play it for very much the same
reason as they play Blood Doll - long-term blood/pool management
option. The alternatives often listed are mostly instant effects; I
believe Doll was favoured for the long term flexibility, not the
instant pool gain.

Second, seeing how the metagame is very hard to predict on a specific
card level, people will always expect to be able to leverage Vessel,
because some people will always play Dolls. Not owning any Vessels,
assuming Vessel is no longer prevalent, or simple force of habit
will likewise motivate to do so.

> I'm not saying whether or not that's currently happening or will
> happen, but that's the theory that Chris is using.

--
Regards,

Daneel

Messages.Author: Daneel
Messages.Body:
On Mon, 3 Nov 2008 14:37:50 -0700, Frederick Scott
<nos...@no.spam.dot.com> wrote:

> On the other hand, if one assumes that Vessels are just too good
> to ever get converted back to Blood Dolls and that pool gain is
> just too important not to pack pretty much the same supply of Vessels
> as one used to pack Blood Dolls, then I think it would be fair to
> suggest that Blood Doll was a better card than it needed to be
> anyway.

i think that in many decks Blood Doll isn't serving as Pool gain. It
serves as blood management. It creates a cushion of pool against
early attacks. My experience is more along the lines of:

You influence out a 7-cap. Put Blood Doll on her. Move off 3 blood in
3 turns - meanwhile, your guy pays for cards, gets into combat, etc.
losing 2 blood. Now your guy has 2 blood, so you push back blood for
the next 2 turns to keep him going (which he more or less spends on
cards, to heal damage, etc.). Net result - you played Blood Doll to
move back 1 blood from your guy, but in the meantime you were
credited as much as 3 pool in the process. So why not play Ascendance
instead, that doesn't cost your vampire 1 blood to gain you 1 pool?
The flexibility and the cushion more than makes up for that blood loss.

Is this a bad thing? I don't think so - in this application Blood Doll
favors toolboxes and slower decks against more focused decks and
faster decks.

--
Regards,

Daneel

> First I beleive Vessel isn't such a terrible card.

It's not. In a vacuum, if it were the only card like it was from day
one, it would be as prevalent as Blood Doll. Even at 1 pool, it is good
in an absolute sense. But relative to Blood Doll, Vessel is mostly just
worse. Except that it kills Blood Dolls. But if it isn't killing Blood

out. Until there are no more Blood Dolls. At which point Vessel seems
less good (even as a trifle). So Vessels start coming out. And so Blood
Dolls start going back in.

Of course maybe it's just the Malkavian prophet in me. ;)

Orpheus

On Tue, 4 Nov 2008, Robert Scythe wrote:

> Nope, just a little bent towards the meth who played it. Yes, very

> effect that can be even more so. Stopping your predator's ousting
> multiple KRC's/Kindred Spirits/Govern's, et al, and protecting
> yourself from the first DI type card played on you can be huge.

Except Dark Influences doesn't protect one from the first cancel card
played. It protects everyone else. The text is: "The next card played
that would cancel another Methuselah's minion card as it is played is
canceled (no cost) and this card is burned instead." If you play Dark
Influences, then you become the only target for everybody else's cancel
cards (unless they don't mind wasting them to burn your Dark Influences).

That seems like a significant balancing factor to me.

Matt Morgan

Does that actually work? Wouldn't skipping a turn from First Tradition
mean no minion phase for which to use Madness Network?

Well, I've never tried grafting Protean onto Malkavians, so haven't
really sat down to see what can be done with it. Just seems like it
wouldn't be such a bad thing, if you're using Protean, to throw a
couple of Homunculi in. Less need of wakes in your deck to let you use
your Misdirections/Counters (and the new Dementation reduce bleed
card).

> Because of the versatility of Dem, or in some other decks because of the
> wonderful titled Malks / !Malks available (a whole other story than titled
> setites, eh ?) !

Maybe, though Presence tends to help out with lack of titles. :)

> > How is it interesting that if I want to have a Thaumaturgy deck that
> > can prevent, I basically have 8 Tremere/!Tremere to choose from before
> > using discipline skills (skipping Kyoko since she has no Thaum to

>

> underlined all the things that For can do for you...

The two points weren't strictly connected. Perhaps I read wrong, but
you were saying that there's an interesting factor in trying to put
together a deck outside the main scope of the clan (Malkavians with
Protean, Tremere that can prevent). It is interesting to do, but there
is very little variety in such decks, due to the extreme low number of
vampires to base such concepts on. Your Tremere/Fortitude deck crypt
will likely look like my Tremere/Fortitude crypt (of the same
groupings), that is what I don't find interesting, because the concept
is so strictly bound. Of course, when you do go through the trouble of
grafting on Fortitude, then I certainly feel you should take advantage
of it, with the good stuff like Freak Drives.

> Well, in a combat environment it could make a difference. You could also use

Right, and if I was making the deck for group 3-4, those would like be

> > It just seems we have different views on what is 'interesting'. I can

>
> Most of the time I try to make something good but original, or original but
> that works. ;)

I'm working on the "that works" part for a lot of my decks :)

> I could adhere to your point if we got good cards making clans like
> !Gangrels more efficient, say some good Cel / Obf cards, that would also
> help Assamites and some overlooked vamps, then I'd say : "ok, that's good,
> let's get those vamps out from the dust !". But if we're talking about
> Trems, Malks or whatever, we already know which ones are good, I don't
> really care for them getting better and better while the rest won't see the
> light of... night anymore !

Well, the discussion has just focused on those two. We haven't seen
the entire set, and don't know what else is has been developed. We
could go on about how a Ventrue wall deck may see some play (at least
around here, I haven't seen anyone make such a deck, even myself). But
there are 5 Ventrue with aus/AUS that I have seen, plus a unique
master giving one +1 intercept.

> I have to underline that here you're just talking about the fads in vamps,

> from new cards making whole strategies obsolete without adding new
> possibilities (just strenghtening already good combos).

Perhaps I'm missing the boat here. One of the main strategies we've
been discussing was Malkavians with Protean. The point of getting
Protean was to be able to Earth Meld. So the strategy was to have a
Malkavian bleed deck that could end combat. I don't see how having No
Trace makes the strategy obsolete. It may make the particular method
obsolete, but the strategy is still there. And even so, inferior Earth
Meld is still better than superior No Trace.

> > And now Nos Princes have an option to
> > play defensively in combat, rather than hoping their offensive combat
> > scares people off.
>
> And if the Ventrue get more Potence they'll have more options. But then
> we'll see less and less difference between clans, and the whole clan /
> disciplines concept will be moot. Which whould be a shame because it's one
> of the pillars of the game.

I can see the concern. And Ventrue are certainly more fighty this time
around. But I don't think that voting Ventrue are going to disappear,
nor power-bleed Ventrue. And fighty Ventrue isn't such an odd concept
even now .. I've made more than one Lucinde Trophy deck. Now I have
more options to go with if I want to continue trying that strategy.

Plus you seem to be a proponent of outside-the-box ways of doing
things. Doesn't a Ventrue Smash kind of deck speak to your inner
creative deck child?

> > I can see the difference, I just don't agree that it's bad. To me,
> > predictability is bad. I shouldn't be able to guess what your deck can
> > do upon seeing one vampire, or one discard. I should be forced to be
> > on my toes. If I see Nossies, I shouldn't be thinking "great, don't
> > have to worry about dealing with bleeds".
>
> Well, it's part of the skill nonetheless. Being able to see the other
> disciplines, wonder why this vampire came out rather than than one, why he
> choses to go Anarch, etc. If you don't need out-of-clans to do special
> things, the game becomes more random, and there is no way that can be good.

Fair enough, I can see this being part of being skilled at the game.
But I don't think it's as bad as you say. Like your response to my
asking if you knew what an Assamite deck might do, you find out fairly
quickly then general idea of the deck you're facing (unless it's not
working as planned, in which case you usually don't need to worry).
But I think there are few decks that you can so assuredly predict in
any case. If Enkidu pops up, you can expect to be fighting, sure, but
the combat options are so varied that you still won't fully know what
to do. He could be hitting fast with blurs, going more a potence
route, using aggravated damage, be a mad rusher, or sit back to block
with animal retainers, and so on and so forth.

> > Yes, there are a lot of good choices. And I do agree with you that
> > people will still use these good vampires with the new cards. I do
> > think though, that we'll be using more of our vampires overall,
> > though, since they can now more easily fit in with some deck ideas.
>

> mostly Toreador and anti, Tremere and anti, and Ventrue, clans which already
> win.

So you don't see Perfect Paragon being a good card to help put
together a Brujah vote deck? Brujah have relatively few titles, so
having an additional vote source is great, plus having some
conditional -intercept to help get those votes off. Of course, Ventrue
and Toreador, already stronger voters, could certainly use the card,
but it's not such a boon for them. They have a lot of vote tools
already, so while having access to another card, though certainly
helpful, I don't think will make them that much more effective than
they already are.

> >> DI is and has always been a no-brainer, it _abstains_ people from
> >> adapting, because it does everything by itself. But it can thwart a
> >> good plan, still all by itself, and now it isn't even possible to
> >> plan it better by keeping another copy of the card in hand. It is a
> >> silver bullet. That cannot be good.
>
> > I can see what you're saying, but I can't really feel sorry for
> > Malkavian bleed decks that are forced to maybe wait an extra turn to
> > oust. I really can't. If your deck is a one-trick pony, that's the
> > price you pay if something gums up the works.
>
> Then how sorry do you feel for the rushers trying to survive the bad evil
> bleeder ? ;)

To be honest, I feel for the rusher .. I've been that rusher far too
many times. So DI2 makes me happier, as it can stem the onslaught for
a turn, and maybe give rushers a bit more of a chance.

> But all the vamps that you'd use only in that type of deck, for that
> purpose, won't see any use anymore (and why use Pre now ? Vote pushing ?
> Already there with Aus, and not much needed with the low-cost titled Malks).

You mentioned attempting Malkavians with Presence, I assumed to make
use of Majesty et al. What vote pushing is there in Auspex?

> More does more. A wall that required, Say, 4 stealth to pass on every action
> will now require 5 or 6. Looks to me like in the recent expansions one
> favours int, then the next stealth, then int, and so on.

So the stealther needs something to maybe survive, since stealth isn't
as reliable and they'll be blocked more ... oh look, combat ends for
Obfuscate! :D

I really, really doubt that wall decks are going to add Eye of Argus
on top of what they use to react with already. I can see them
_replacing_ some cards with Eyes. But it is conditional. Sure, I get
+1 more intercept (overall, provided Eyes replaced something like
Precognition) on those bleeds and rushes, but now I have -1 intercept
(overall) on those votes, hunts, equips/recruits, rescues ... Seems
like a balance to me.

> > The most likely use of the card is the superior, which gives you a
> > Wake without the drawback. But then, it should be more potent, as it
> > requires AUS, rather than being disciplineless. It'll also help out
> > clans who have aus out-of-clan, in better defending themselves.
>
> It's a good card, no doubt ! But it's a rise in the power curve (from what
> we've seen of this set, currently in favour of intercept).

Not a bad thing in my books. The last few tournaments and drafts,
stealth bleed has been the winner, because stealth is much more
prevalent than intercept.

> Sure. But I'd say this isn't a bleed card at all, as they already had access
> to as much bleed with Computer Hacking (efficient with weenie Obf, or
> possibly Nossies). This is a polyvalent card, useful in an ANI rush deck for
> the occasional bleed boost. So what I really mean by "far from it" is that
> it doesn't get the nossies any closer to competing with the bleeders,
> really. But it might just make their Ani (wall with rush or plain rush)
> midcap decks a little more viable.

A good point. But I don't see a problem with this. One of the big
'complaints' I hear about combat decks is that they're great as
smashing minions, but weak on actually ousting. Giving such decks a
bit more versatility to get some ousting power is a boon, I think.

> >>> Assamites and Gangrel.
>
> >> I don't see the link with those 2 ??
>
> > Assamites now make strong stealth/bleeders ...
>
> Strong maybe not, but viable. Ok.

Consistent bleeds of 3 at stealth isn't strong? Nevermind having
Khabar: Glory out and getting 4 additional pool when you oust. I
nearly killed my prey with a Loss deck, and only lost because I had a
Loss deck bleeding me.

> > While some cards do add new abilities to disciplines, it's hard to
> > tell if such cards will really have that huge an impact. While I can
> > certainly see No Trace adding to Malkavian decks, evidence has shown
> > that Malkavian decks have done just fine without such combat defense.
>
> Sure. It does, though, depend very much on the environment. To give you a
> personnal example : in november, 2006 I made second in the ECQ (the biggest
> tournie of the year in Europe) with a Dem deck ; then I sort of dropped from
> the game (no time) ; in september 2007 I still tried the french LCQ, with
> the same sort of deck, and made... 1 VP !! Why ? Well, the local and current
> metagame had shifted to casual bruise, meaning not much dedicated combat
> with Psyche or IG, but lots of Ani fight, rushing allies etc. And I just had
> my ass handed to me on a plate !! If I had access to a S:CE card at the time
> (and if I had the means to anticipate it, which in that precise example
> wasn't the case) it would have possibly made a huge difference !

A fair point .. but then how would your performance the first time
around have gone, where those combat ends would have just been
clogging your hand? You had options for combat defense as it was, and
chose to forego them (of course, they're not as effective as combat
ends). I do get your point, and I think you have a point in that
Malkavian decks will likely have some more survivability with No
Trace. Will it be such that they'll be winning a lot more? Simply
can't tell right now.

> > The same for Rego Motus for Tremere, though again (despite personal
> > experience), they have stood up relatively well without prevent. Will
> > these cards make these decks stronger? More than likely. But it's not
> > as if these are totally foreign concepts, it'll just now be easier to
> > build such deck concepts, especially for those with smaller card
> > pools.
>
> Yes. Easier. No-brainer. Concepts with out-of-clan = dead. Me no like.

Well, I don't think a lot of out-of-clan concepts are dead. Perhaps
not used as much, as there are easier and broader options now for some
strategies. But I think people will still try things, or make use of
new vampires (if there are any) with older strategies.

Plus, I think some of these cards open up _new_ strategies. Ventrue
now have some fighting and blocking potential. Tremere don't have to
rely so much on Theft to keep themselves alive in heavier combats,
which opens up different thaumaturgy combat strategies. Brujah can
look at trying to get into the voting arena. And so on and so forth.

It seems that you're more against the potential loss of deck building
challenges, of putting together a deck with limited resources and
trying to make it work. Since when these strategies are brought in-
clan/discipline, you are raising flags over the flattening of things.

> > Even the cards I thought
> > were "holy cow, what were they thinking", on reflection, simply strong
> > cards, and not the end of the game a we know it.
>
> If anything for me anounces such a Gehenna, it's not just one card, but the
> general trend I can foresee from a whole lot of cards.
>
> Of course maybe it's just the Malkavian prophet in me. ;)

Well, as we both agreed upon, only time will tell, once we see the
entire set, and start playing with the cards and seeing just how
effective the new cards are.

While I can agree that we'll see out-of-clan strategies becoming less
common, I see those strategies becoming 'in-clan', and thus appearing
in greater variety. Some strategies will become weaker, while other
concepts will have some more support.

Chris, Thrall of Arika

> out. Until there are no more Blood Dolls. At which point Vessel seems

> Dolls start going back in.

You give the very reason, though, that Vessels won't come out. In the
absence of BD, the card "would be as prevalent as Blood Doll." Vessel
has one close substitute - BD. It has plenty of substitutes that
aren't so close - Minion Tap, Villein, Tribute, Ascendance, Grooming
the Protege, etc. Remove BD from the game, and Vessel just moves in,
taking over the role almost entirely because nothing else does the job
anywhere near as good - can claim that Vessel's cost is prohibitive to
certain decks, except that's easily remedied by playing Villein with
Vessel, which may mean not as many Vessels as BDs in games but still
means a constant presence of them.

So, why expect BD to make a comeback?

I'm willing to believe there are places where Vessel never establishes
itself as the dominate BD play, though I'm sure that the lack of
ownership of sufficient quantities of Vessel has had something to do
with Vessel not moving in as quickly as it should have in many places,
to where BD will remain a viable option in those places. But, once
Vessel establishes itself, I don't see where people will suddenly
decide to stop playing it because there aren't BDs around any longer
to nuke. Rather, I'd expect some tweaking on other cards - adding
other pool gain on top of the Vessels - and/or more attempts to take
advantage of what Vessel does better - trifleness, untap combos.

For amusement, one suggestion I've heard is that Blood Doll should
have the ability to blow up Vessel - leveling the playing field and
creating all sorts of havoc.

Messages.Author: Chris Berger
Messages.Body:
On Nov 6, 7:11 am, jwjbwhe...@gmail.com wrote:
>
> But even in a worst-case scenario, Blood Doll is a versatile Minion-
> Tap-for-One that that you have the option of using as a Gird-Minions-
> for-One.  That's not such a terrible effect, and the hope that you may
> use it twice, three times, or more, before it blows up, makes it even
> better.
>

Exactly. Blood Doll lets you use it *immediately*. That's good. Of
course, it's not necessarily worth the MPA and card if you only use it
for one. But it still works like a combination Ascendance that costs
a blood with an alternate textline of Life in the City that costs a
pool. Neither use by itself would be strong, but you pay for
versatility, and if it were a Trifle that worked that way, just one, I
suspect it would be considered an okay card that's maybe slightly
below the power curve.

But how often does your Blood Doll get blown up *immediately* by a
Vessel. Say that your predator and prey each have 8 Vessels in their
decks (seems like a lot - I would much prefer something 4 Vessels, and
if I need more pool gain masters, 4 of Blood Doll or a Minion Tap-like
card). There is something like a 10% chance that one of them has a
Vessel in hand at any time (I didn't do the actual math, because it's
complicated and the exact number is not important. Let's say that
it's certainly between 5 and 20%). So your Blood Dolls are *not*
getting blown up immediately. Most of the time (at least 80%), your
Blood Dolls should make it to turn 2, and 3 turns is not at all a
stretch. Plus, if you actually need the Blood Doll to stay alive,
only your predator is really a risk to pop it.

The problem with Blood Doll before that it was good pool gain that
could be used over-and-over again, could never be removed, and could
double as push blood whenever you felt like it. It was obviously too
versatile when it was printed for the fact that it would never be
burned, which is why you used to see it in like 50-80% of decks. Even
as it is, you are likely to get about 3 turns of usage out of a Blood
Doll, in my experience. The density of Vessels will move the average
up or down, but never below 1. So, how many turns do you need to get
out of a Blood Doll for it to be good? Obviously, 1 turn is a little
weak. 2 turns is useful, but I tend to believe it doesn't pass the
"Ascendance test" (i.e. is this non-trifle master card better than
Ascendance? If not, play Ascendance instead). After 3 turns, you
have gotten as much blood back from the vampire as Grooming the
Protege without needing a younger uncontrolled vampire, or you have
pushed up 3 blood to keep your vamp from hunting (more expensive than
a hunting ground, but you got to use it the first turn), or you pulled
back only when you needed to and pushed only when you needed to,
etc... All in all, after 3 turns, I think you got your money's
worth. This may be where I differ from the people that want BD to
last forever-and-ever-amen. Do you think 3 turns of Blood Doll isn't
worth a master phase action?

> > Rather, I'd expect some tweaking on other cards - adding
> > other pool gain on top of the Vessels - and/or more
> > attempts to take advantage of what Vessel does better -
> > trifleness, untap combos.
>
> Like Vessel + Jake Washington?  Yes, you'd expect to see such things
> depending on the specifics of deck-design and strategy.

Vessel is good in those decks specifically designed to do stuff in the
untap. Danielle Diron particularly likes Vessel. But in the absence
of Blood Dolls, Vessel just isn't good. Paying a pool and not getting
to use it until next turn essentially costs 2 pool more than Blood
Doll. Sure, it's a Trifle, so I would also use it in decks that don't
have the master card space for Blood Dolls due to needing that space
to "make the deck go". But even with Vessel in existence, there are
still a lot of decks that I'd rather play Blood Dolls in. If you can
pop a Blood Doll controlled by your prey, then Vessel is very strong.
If you can't, I just don't see how it's worth the pool, when there are
other pool gain options out there.

Of course, I tend to not think more than 5 turns into the future -
assuming that any card that takes 5 turns to pay off isn't worth it
because my game could be over. Thus why I don't see 3 turns of Blood
Doll being a problem (I could be dead in 5 turns anyway), or why I see
Vessel as not very good (after 5 turns of Vessel you have -4 blood and
+3 pool, after only 3 turns of Blood Doll you have -3 blood and +3
pool). That certainly isn't universally true, and it's one of the
reasons that I thought Spell of Life was terrible when I first saw
it. "It takes 5 turns, and I could be dead by then with nothing to
show for it. Even if I get 1 every turn and none of them are blocked,
I only get 1 turn to use the Mummies..." I think I was definitely
wrong on that. I have a Spell of Life deck that, while the jury's
still out on whether it's any good or not, is definitely fun to play
and with a non-terrible draw can wreak some havoc.

But yeah, maybe it's the 5 turn thing that makes my perspective a
little different on this. How long is the average game? Something
like 10-14 turns per player. If I get Vessel in my opening draw and
get a vampire out at the end of turn 2 (not guaranteed), then I would
play it on turn 3 and start using it on turn 4 to get 6-10 turns use
out of it. That's certainly worth it, and the difference between
Vessel and Blood Doll in that long of a time frame is much smaller.
Vessel is still *worse* than a Blood Doll, assuming each is played in
a vacuum. But even getting it that early, the number is still not a
*lot* more than 5 turns (going by my earlier definition that 5 turns
of Vessel starts the turn you play it, it's technically 7-11 turns of
it). And you can't guarantee getting it in your opening hand, even
with 8 of them in the deck. In general, for cards with payoff-over-
time, I prefer to think of the game in 5 turn chunks (if I play this
card, where will I be 4 turns later?), because you never know if
you'll get more time than that.

My contention is that, in that time frame, Vessel is not particularly
great unless it can blow up a Blood Doll controlled by your prey, and
conversely, Blood Doll is still good even *if* it gets blown up by a
Vessel.

>> yourself from the first DI type card played on you can be huge.

>
> Except Dark Influences doesn't protect one from the first cancel card
> played. It protects everyone else. The text is: "The next card played
> that would cancel another Methuselah's minion card as it is played is
> canceled (no cost) and this card is burned instead." If you play Dark
> Influences, then you become the only target for everybody else's cancel
> cards (unless they don't mind wasting them to burn your Dark Influences).
>
> That seems like a significant balancing factor to me.

The signigicant balacing factor seems to *me* that it costs twice as much as
pool as DI does. Two pool is enough to make people discard hunting grounds,
intercept locations or equipment when they're low-ish on pool.
If it would *also* make you the "DI-target", so to speak, I can't really
imagine anyone playing it. Ever. The "can't play again this turn" clause,
while handy, isn't really *that* strong to warrant the extra disadvantage on
top of the double cost. Why wouldn't you just play a DI and then not having
to deal with getting rid of the card first before you can play another?
